doc.title: Loren Schoenberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019

chapter: Benny Goodman and the big band
title: After Goodman: no ghost band, MusicMasters albums
summary: After Goodman's death he declined a ghost band and recorded albums using Moscow-tour commissions.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: I was gone. My place was taken by Ted Nash. And I’ll say now, you know, thirty-five years, thirty-four years retrospect, Ted’s a better section player than I am you know. But that was a life lesson, you know what I mean? And then Benny died the following June and I mean I kept doing gigs with the band anyway, when I had gigs, and Benny passed away and then I decided soon after there that this was not going to be a Benny Goodman ghost band. I mean (a) his estate eventually said there will be no ghost band. But I really had no desire to go down the road like some other band leaders did. I mean I played Carnegie Hall with Bob Wilber on the Fiftieth Anniversary of the Carnegie Hall concert. I had no desire to go down that (a) I don’t play the clarinet, (b) without Ken Peplowski or a handful of, I mean young guys from my generation back 35 years ago there were not © Fillius Jazz Archive -24-

that many who you’d want to hear play a Benny Goodman concert, because it would suck. I mean there are a handful, but not that many. And I didn’t know them you know. So I gave that up and then started recording our own albums and we did four or five albums for MusicMasters. And they were nice combinations of, I mean I’m no great arranger. I can arrange — the most arranging I ever did was for Bobby Short during the years when I had his band. But with my own big band, no. I mean I wanted much better writers than me. So eventually James Chirillo and Mark Lopeman and Mike Christiansen arranged, plus Mel and others who were in the band said you know when Benny took the band to Moscow in 1962 he commissioned Tadd Dameron and Bob Brookmeyer and Johnny Carisi and a few other people to write all this great music, the majority of which never was recorded. So we started recording those things. And we made a series of records starting in 198- well the first one was ’84 then the second version of the band in 1987 through, for about ten years we made a record every couple of years. Eventually Steve Wilson came in the band and other great players. So anyway that’s —
Well you are one of the luckiest guys in the world then.
